Question B-007-001-008.

Why the correct answer is right: Of the listed amateur bands, 160 metres has the lowest frequency and longest wavelength. Ground wave generally reaches farther at the lower frequency end of the comparison.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "40 metres": This band can have useful high-frequency (HF) propagation, but its higher frequency gives it less ground-wave reach than 160 metres.
- sourceIndex 2: "10 metres": Ten metres is near the top of HF, where ordinary ground wave is much less effective than on the lowest band listed.
- sourceIndex 3: "6 metres": Six metres is in the very high frequency (VHF) range. Normal work there is dominated by line-of-sight and special openings rather than the best ground-wave distance.
